I wrote the S1 area spec for Orders, Invoicing and Shipping at /home/cloudcli/sourcecode/access-excel-to-django/northwind/analysis/rules/orders.json and orders.md. The JSON has kind area, spec_version 1.0 and signed null. All four acceptance commands passed.

What the file holds:
- **Rules:** 50, numbered R-orders-001 to 050. 38 are proven by rule tests, 9 by equivalence units and 3 end to end.
- **Objects:** all 323 objects in scope, 202 keep and 121 drop. Each one is named exactly as in inventory.json. rules-coverage counts all 323 as covered (323 of the 547 in the whole inventory).
- **Other content:** 8 lookups, 16 relations, workflow order_to_ship, 11 services and 12 open questions (Q-orders-001 to 012).

The order rules follow the life cycle New → Invoiced → Shipped → Paid → Closed:
- Invoicing needs a New order with at least one line, all lines Allocated, and a shipping fee filled in.
- Shipping needs an Invoiced order plus shipped date, shipper and fee. Payment needs a Shipped order plus payment method and paid date. Closing needs a Paid order and a confirmation.
- An order can only be deleted while New or Invoiced, and its lines can only be edited while it is New.
- Which order fields can be edited depends on the status.
- When a line is saved it is marked Allocated or No Stock, and stock allocation runs again for the products it touches.

The invoice rule spells out the line and total arithmetic. Tax is charged on the subtotal only when the order is Taxable, and shipping is not taxed.

The company and employee rules cover:
- **Delete and type-change blocks:** a company with orders or purchase orders cannot be deleted or change type; an employee with orders, purchase orders, staff or privileges cannot be deleted.
- **Other company and employee rules:** an employee cannot supervise themselves; names must be unique; phone numbers follow a fixed format.

The other area-wide rules are:
- A required-field check on saving.
- Audit stamping from the 13 data macros.
- A start-up rule with trigger schedule:startup, sourced from the AutoExec macro. It shifts the sample dates forward once, on first run.

Sign-in and privileges objects are kept, with target_component foundation:sign-in or foundation:roles. Access-only plumbing is dropped: ribbon, recently-used list, message texts, error log, demo-data admin tools, and the welcome, help and about screens. The must_keep item "order entry → invoice (printable PDF) → shipping" is kept as workflow order_to_ship, and rptInvoice is kept as orders.reports.
notes: There was no answers.md, so every assumption is recorded as an open question with its default: Q-orders-001 to Q-orders-012 in orders.json and orders.md. They cover the printed invoice date versus the stored invoice date, the absence of any date-order checks, tax not charged on shipping, the 20-most-recent order list for an employee, keeping the first-run date shift, the company save confirmation, the cascade when a company is deleted, the dropped Access conveniences (export to Excel, label wizard, map link, recently-used list), the default order list filter, the US phone format, a new company defaulting to tax exempt, and having no partial invoices.

Assumption: the 13 BeforeChange data macros all do the same audit stamping (created-by/on and modified-by/on, with the created values protected on update). They are kept with target_component foundation:audit-fields, and rule R-orders-031 cites them. The engagement's foundation lists only sign-in and roles, so S4 (or S1.synthesize) has to take on audit-field stamping. The other areas' data macros (Products, PurchaseOrders and so on) are the same and should get the same target.

Assumption: the AutoExec start-up becomes R-orders-049 with trigger schedule:startup and target orders.jobs. Per contracts §14, S5 will create a one-off management command for it: a first-run job that shifts every date forward by the gap between the latest order date and today, then sets the first-run flag. S1.area.inventory.summary:
Wrote the S1 rules for the Products and Inventory area (id inventory, kept). The rules file analysis/rules/inventory.json has kind area, signed null and spec_version 1.0. It holds 30 rules, R-inventory-001 to 030. Test kinds: 23 rule, 5 equivalence and 2 e2e (R-010 for the stock-count mismatch prompt, R-030 for restocking end to end).

The rules cover:
- how the stock figures are calculated: physical stock, allocated, no-stock, on-order, quantity to sell and the suggested reorder quantity
- how stock is allocated to order lines, oldest order first
- stock takes: date set by the system, expected quantity recorded, no negative counts, append-only, and allocation re-runs when one is saved
- product validation, and product codes built from a prefix, the category code and the product number
- when a category code is locked, and when a category or product can be deleted
- the reorder flow: open an outstanding PO instead, require a vendor, choose the quantity, add to the vendor's oldest New PO or create a new one
- discontinued products and what the product page shows
- the product list, the export, the order and PO history tabs and the order-line product pickers
- audit stamps from the 4 data macros, and product-vendor links being unique

All 85 objects in scope are decided: 68 keep and 17 drop. The drops are Access UI plumbing (requery and refresh, lazy loading, the recently-used list, an empty help handler) and the unused qryMaxStockTakeDate. Every kept rule-bearing object is either cited by a rule or has a reason saying it holds no rule; rules-coverage against inventory.json shows no uncovered object from this area.

The file also has 3 lookups, 6 relations, 2 workflows (inventory_restock, which carries the must-keep 'inventory levels and restocking', and stock_take), 5 services and 8 open questions. analysis/rules/inventory.md is the reader version with the same content.
